Jerome H. Powell: Given the current low inflation and elevated unemployment, the Committee should consider lowering the federal funds rate at its next meeting to support economic recovery and promote our dual mandate. Proactive accommodation is appropriate to address ongoing economic challenges.

Given the elevated unemployment rate and inflation below target, it is appropriate for the Committee to begin easing policy now to support the economic recovery. Waiting for more data risks delaying necessary accommodation that can help achieve our dual mandate.

Given the elevated unemployment rate and inflation below target, it is not urgent to reduce the current level of policy accommodation. Our focus remains on supporting the economy and labor market recovery until substantial progress is made.

Given the ongoing fiscal restraint and the unemployment rate still elevated above pre-pandemic levels, it is not urgent to reduce the current level of policy accommodation, as inflation remains below target and the economy needs continued support. Given the current economic conditions with inflation below target and elevated unemployment, I would support a 25 basis point cut at the coming meeting to provide additional accommodation and support the recovery. It is important to act proactively to foster a stronger labor market and move inflation toward our 2% goal.

Given the ongoing economic challenges and below-target inflation, the time has not yet come to dial back policy restraint; maintaining accommodative monetary policy remains essential to support recovery. Michelle W. Bowman: Given that inflation remains below target and the unemployment rate is elevated, the Committee should maintain the current federal funds rate to support continued economic recovery rather than lowering it further at the next meeting. Given the ongoing economic uncertainty and inflation persistently below target, the Committee should wait for more data before considering easing policy to ensure the recovery is on a sustainable path. Premature easing risks undermining progress toward our dual mandate goals.

Given the ongoing economic disruption and elevated unemployment, it is not urgent to reduce the current level of policy accommodation. Maintaining supportive monetary policy remains essential to foster a sustained and inclusive recovery.
